claim.quote: The ARGO-YBJ air shower detector monitored the Crab Nebula gamma ray emission from 2007 November to 2013 February.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published in Astrophys. J. 798, 119 (2015).

name: Crab Nebula: five-year observation with ARGO-YBJ

official_url.quote: Crab Nebula: five-year observation with ARGO-YBJ

significance.quote: reached the statistical significance of 21.1 standard deviations

summary.plain: ARGO-YBJ watched the Crab Nebula for more than five years and measured its TeV gamma-ray spectrum from 0.3 to 20 TeV. The signal reached 21.1 standard deviations, and the emission looked steady over the five years.
summary.technical: Integrated signal of about 3.3 × 10⁵ events at 21.1 standard deviations; spectrum in 0.3-20 TeV fitted by a power law with index 2.63 ± 0.05; 200-day light curve compatible with steady emission; no flare above four standard deviations in a 1-15 day search.

title: Crab Nebula: five-year observation with ARGO-YBJ
why_it_matters: The abstract reports a five-year energy spectrum and light curve of the Crab Nebula, a standard candle of TeV astronomy, and a correlation analysis with Fermi-LAT over about 4.5 years.
